title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Eleanor Chen
description: Context: our continuous batcher scheduler occasionally allowed long-tail queueing where large or badly-shaped requests could starve smaller latency-sensitive requests. This led to customer incidents (see linked Linear ENG-3141) and noisy p99 regressions on mixed workloads. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention, and introduce per-queue timeouts and metrics. Changes are behind an opt-in runtime flag (experimental.scheduler_tuning_v2) so we can rollout gradually. Motivation: reduce p99 latency for small/interactive requests without sacrificing throughput for bulk workloads. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a dual-queue strategy in the continuous scheduler that separates latency-sensitive and throughput-oriented requests and allows proportional service (fairness weights) between queues. 2) Add a starvation detector that tracks per-request wait time and elevates priority when a configured threshold is reached. 3) Add per-queue and per-request timeouts (configurable) with graceful cancellation and retry hooks. 4) Add telemetry: new metrics (batcher.queue_length, batcher.queue_wait_seconds_bucketed, batcher.starvation_elevations, batcher.timeout_evictions) and tracing spans to observe queueing decisions. 5) Tune default batching windows and backpressure thresholds to avoid pathological batching of very long sequences. 6) Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for scheduler invariants, integration tests simulating mixed workloads, and perf harness results included. Rollout plan: feature flag default off; enable in canary region for 24h with traffic shaping; evaluate p99 and throughput metrics; progressively expand. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + perf plan (linked Linear: ENG-3141, ENG-3290) - [x] Implementation behind feature flag - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmark harness run and results included - [x] Observability + dashboards updated - [x] Docs + changelog entry Impact: internal-only runtime feature by default; no breaking API changes. Measured results (perf harness on t4-based cluster, mixed small/large seq workload): p50 unchanged, p95 ~+5% (acceptable), p99 reduced from 120ms -> 86ms for latency-sensitive class, overall throughput within 3% of baseline. Related: linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3141, linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3290. Notes: one flaky integration test was addressed by adding a deterministic scheduler seed in tests. See CI notes below.
